The actual FileSuite simple-write test sequences drained writes and reads with append, and asserts the round-trip content. This is evidence of test construction only; it was not executed.
Final source preserves per-input Unit emissions and documents them. This confirms the narrowed revision rather than the initial all-sinks draining proposal.
The actual flatMap implementation requires the diagnostic witness and delegates to Pull.flatMapOutput. The protection concerns the static output type, not a guarantee of nonempty streams.

Despite the adjacent per-line Unit emission documentation, lines delegates to the draining foreach implementation and returns INothing. Treat documentation as inconsistent, not as a positive cardinality oracle.
The 3.0-targeted sink proposal still uses CE2.2.0-RC3. The build defines io/test and coreJVM/test via testJVM; commands must not be projected onto newer cross-project layouts.

claims.rule: Before replacing an FS2 sink or changing its result type, distinguish zero emissions, one completion emission, and one Unit per input; inspect downstream flatMap/>>/take and use append only when continuation should run after successful exhaustion independently of emissions.
claims.applicability: Historical review of #1754/#1913, with the final change targeted to FS2 3.0 while the inspected branch still depended on CE2.2.0-RC3. For current code inspect the actual sink signature and implementation. NotNothing prevents some statically empty binds, not every empty Stream[F, Unit].
claims.counterexample: A Queue.enqueue emitting one Unit per enqueued element intentionally supports take(n); draining it and moving take after the drain changes termination. A widened empty stream can still silently skip a flatMap continuation.
